title: Architectural Plans
description: Components of architectural plans including perspective drawings, lot or site development plans, location or vicinity maps, floor plans, doors, windows, jamb parts, identification marks, wall thickness, scales, and required floor-plan information.

content.text: Architectural plans communicate the design, dimensions, arrangement, and construction information of a building.
A perspective drawing presents a three-dimensional view of a building. It helps communicate how the building may appear when viewed from a particular position.

items: Provides a clearer understanding of the proposed design.

reviewer.title: Lot Plan or Site Development Plan

content.text: A lot plan or site development plan shows the building in relation to the property boundaries and other site features.

items: May indicate setbacks and open spaces.
Shows the relationship of the building to the site.

content.text: A location plan or vicinity map indicates where the property is located in relation to surrounding streets, landmarks, and other areas.

items: Identifies the general location of the property.

content.text: A floor plan is a scaled drawing showing the arrangement of spaces within a building. It commonly indicates walls, doors, windows, rooms, dimensions, and other architectural information.
Doors are represented in architectural plans using symbols and dimensions. Door information helps identify the size and location of openings.
Windows are identified by their dimensions and marks. The jamb is part of the frame surrounding an opening and is important in describing door and window construction.

reviewer.title: Door Jamb, Identification Marks, and Wall Thickness

content.text: Architectural drawings use identification marks and dimensions to communicate construction information clearly. Wall thickness must also be represented accurately in floor plans.

items: Door and window identification marks help distinguish different types.
Wall thickness must be represented in the plan.
Dimensions should be clear and readable.
A consistent scale should be used.
